findings.note: The single daily-preparations control already exists (choice.daily = true, and Builder.tsx renders nothing for a choice askedAtDailyPrep). What was missing is the GRANT: dailyChoiceGrants (derive.ts:1824) reads `opt.grant` off the record's own options and every option here carried none, so the morning's answer was recorded and nothing was cast. The whole `choice` value is re-emitted because a member of one field cannot be patched. The build-time duplicate lives in src/rules/featCantripGrants.ts (FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS['kitsune-spell-familiarity']) and is a CROSS-FILE GAP, not a row.

The grant now names `figment` and the label reads Figment; the option's `value` stays "ghost-sound" because it is the stored answer key and it is also the word feat-2619 prints. The sibling nagaji row already had this shape (print says "mage hand", the option is telekinetic-hand).

findings.note: No picker, exactly as the owner ruled: the archetype's prerequisite is "You have a spellcasting class feature", so the tradition of the spells used to meet it IS the character's own class casting. `traditionFromCasting` is the existing field for that sentence (types.ts:2494) and has a reader at build.ts:8243 — `(g.traditionFromCasting ? caster?.tradition : undefined) ?? g.tradition ?? spell.traditions[0]` — where `caster` is the character's prepared/spontaneous entry. No `tradition` fallback is authored because the prerequisite forbids the not-a-caster case; without this the fallback was the spell's own first tradition, which is arcane for time-sense.

backfillRows.why: feat-8480 prints "You also gain time sense as an innate cantrip usable at will. This innate spell and your focus spells from the time mage archetype are of the same tradition as the spells you used to meet the archetype's prerequisites." The shipped grant was `[{spellId:'time-sense',atWill:true}]` with no tradition, so build.ts fell through to the spell's first tradition (arcane) and a divine cleric's Time Sense read arcane. The superseded row's whole value is carried through; only `traditionFromCasting` is added.

findings.note: NO ROW — no reader exists for the printed condition, and authoring one would ship dead data while deleting the live toggle would take the resistance away entirely. The clause gates on the WORN ARMOUR'S CATEGORY. `IwrEntry` (types.ts:480-539) carries minLevel / whenCreatureTrait / unlessCreatureTrait / whenVoidHealing / against / condition and nothing about armour, and the deriveDefenses resistance loop (derive.ts:2786-2818) honours exactly those gates. The formula route is closed too: `FormulaScope` is {level, abilities, speeds, archetypeFeats} (derive.ts:2275) and substituteTokens leaves any other @token in place so the value resolves to 0. The fact itself IS on the sheet — `findWornArmor(c, db).armor.category` — so this is a reader gap, not a data gap; see CROSS-FILE GAPS and DATA STILL NEEDED in the report for the exact code change and the two rows that must land WITH it (never before it).

A delete, not a move: both Strikes are ALREADY on the stances that print them (core.stances['claw-stance'].strikes = frenzied claw 1d6 slashing, core.stances['talon-stance'].strikes = Spinning Talon 1d8 slashing), and deriveStrikes renders the active stance's own strikes at derive.ts:5155. build.ts's `collectGrantedNaturals` skips a feat's grantedStrikes only when the FEAT ITSELF is a stance with a stance definition (build.ts:2881-2884); the dedication is `['archetype','dedication']` with no `content.stances['clawdancer-dedication']`, so its copies were never skipped and surfaced permanently, beside the stance's copy. `grantsActions: ['claw-stance','talon-stance']` is untouched — that is the lane that puts the two stance toggles on the Main tab.

findings.note: One `choice` row carries BOTH of this record's choice-side changes, because two findings on the same record+field must be one row: the 8th-level gate (this finding) and the removal of `distinctAcrossTakes` (versatile-mutation#takable-twice — that flag only ever served a second taking of this feat, which print does not allow). The bludgeoning-or-slashing clause needs no option: print makes it a per-use decision at the table ("When you Spit Ambient Magic, you CAN CHOOSE to have the ostilli deal bludgeoning or slashing damage instead of piercing"), not a build answer. ⚠ `FeatChoiceDef.minLevel` has a reader on the DAILY path only (dailyChoices.ts:53); the build-time path ignores it — see CROSS-FILE GAPS.

backfillRows.why: feat-5454 prints "At 8th level, choose one of the following: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage; when your ostilli Spits Ambient Magic, it can deal that damage type instead and adds that trait to the action." The shipped choice asked the five-option question at 4th level with no gate, four levels before the character is entitled to any of its answers. `minLevel: 8` is the field FeatChoiceDef already declares for "the character level from which this question is asked at all". `distinctAcrossTakes` is dropped in the same value because the same document prints no Special clause allowing a second taking (see the maxTakable row). The superseded row's whole value (flag/prompt/kind/options) is merged in unchanged.

findings.note: `maxTakable` absent reads as 1 through `maxTakes()` (featGrants.ts:881-884), so deleting the field is the whole fix — no replacement value is needed. The `distinctAcrossTakes` half of this finding rides on the `choice` row above (same record, same field as versatile-mutation#energy-level, so it must be one row). The second row strips the SOURCE of the false flag: the shipped description carried a Special clause that is in no printed document, so removing the flag alone would have left the player reading a promise the builder no longer keeps. Both rows are pathless, as a description row must be.

backfillRows.why: feat-5454's full printed text ends "...and adds that trait to the action." — there is no Special clause, and a corpus grep of the AoN mirror's feat documents for "second time at 16th level" finds none. The record shipped `maxTakable: 2`, letting the feat be taken twice on nothing but invented text. Deleted; `maxTakes()` reads an absent field as 1.

feat-5454's whole body is "Your ostilli's darts can deal different types of damage. When you Spit Ambient Magic, you can choose to have the ostilli deal bludgeoning or slashing damage instead of piercing damage. At 8th level, choose one of the following: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage; when your ostilli Spits Ambient Magic, it can deal that damage type instead and adds that trait to the action." Our description appended a "**Special** You can take this feat a second time at 16th level..." paragraph that appears in no document in the AoN mirror — it is the text the false `maxTakable: 2` was read from. Restored to the printed body, verbatim.

findings.note: Only the wrong grant is a row. The two proficiency halves have no data carrier at all: no feat in public/core.json carries any weapon-category proficiency field (the only weapon-ish keys on any feat record are untrainedProficiency / critSpecWeapons / weaponTraits / untrainedWeaponProficiency), and the trained-in-advanced-weapons grant this feat DOES deliver lives in the code registry src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts as `'arcana-of-iron': { weapon: { advanced: 'trained' } }`. The conditional expert step therefore belongs in that registry beside it — see CROSS-FILE GAPS.
